subject: Latency gating & probe windows — hosted swap feasibility
thread:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Chu <ethan.chu@integron.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency gating & probe windows — hosted swap feasibility

Ethan,

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on the high-level ask. Short recap and concrete next steps to get us to a hosted vs incumbent latency decision:

Summary notes (high level)
- Target acceptance: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms end-to-end for your token mix (current baseline per call).
- Streaming: you have a mix of short streaming requests (avg 8 tokens) and multi-chunk sessions for interactive workflows; concurrency per instance is a key constraint.
- Incumbent baseline: you noted ~p95 170ms / p99 400ms under normal traffic; retained for context.

What we need from Integron for an apples-to-apples probe
1) Representative traffic profile (CSV attached: integron_p95_traffic_profile.csv) — token distribution, request shapes, % streaming vs non-streaming, and peak QPS windows.
2) A small auth token and endpoint allowlist for our test harness (we will use a read-only test key).
3) If possible, a short recording of a multi-chunk session or a sample payload with chunk timing (~1–2 examples).

Redwood probe proposal (what we will run)
- Two 90-minute windows (can be contiguous): one simulating your normal envelope, one simulating a 1.5x peak to stress tail behavior.
- Metrics captured: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, server-side queueing, connection concurrency, streaming chunk reassembly latency, and token-decoding CPU/GPU utilization.
- Baseline comparisons: run identical probe against your incumbent (if you can provide a test endpoint) or compare to your supplied baseline CSV.

Preliminary hosted fit knobs we plan to exercise
- batch size caps and continuous-batching profile
- streaming chunk prefetching and small-chunk aggregation
- KV cache prefixing to reduce prefix decoding costs for repeat sessions

Attachments: integron_p95_traffic_profile.csv, probe-schedule.ics, hosted-fit-quick-matrix.xlsx

Proposed immediate next steps
- You share the CSV + sample payloads by EOD Friday (June 5).
- Redwood schedules the first 90-minute probe for week of June 8 — tentative slots in probe-schedule.ics.
- We’ll share a short smoke script (one-click harness) for you to run on your side if you prefer to host the probe endpoint.

If that plan looks good we’ll lock a slot and Ben will own the execution runbook.

Best,
Naomi

Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency gating & probe windows — hosted swap feasibility

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear ask. A few clarifications from our SRE/infra side: 

- Current observed baseline (incumbent): p95=168ms, p99=395ms (these numbers are 95th/99th from our production aggregator for the last 7 days).
- Streaming concurrency: typical per-host concurrency is 24 long-lived streams, short bursts up to ~120 concurrent short requests across the cluster.
- Tokenization: we have a bimodal token distribution — 70% < 16 tokens, 25% 16–128, 5% > 128 (we’ll confirm exact CSV).

Questions: 
1) For the 1.5x peak test, will you ramp or step? We prefer a stepped ramp (3 x 30-minute buckets) so we can see when tail degrades.
2) Do you require a dedicated test key and IP allowlist? We can provide both but need a short legal addendum for test-only activity.

We’ll upload the requested CSV and two sample multi-chunk session traces by EOD Thursday.

Ethan
Ethan Chu
SRE Manager, Integron Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Chu <ethan.chu@integron.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 13:40:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency gating & probe windows — hosted swap feasibility

Ethan — quick responses inline and a tightening of the probe plan: 

On streaming concurrency: we typically test both sustained and spiky concurrency. For hosted qualification we recommend:
- Sustained concurrency target: 60 concurrent streams at steady-state to represent cluster-level headroom.
- Spike scenario: short 3–5 minute spikes up to 180 concurrent short requests (this replicates burst behavior you described).

On ramping vs stepped: stepped ramp is fine — we’ll run 3 x 30-minute buckets (baseline / 1.25x / 1.5x) but will also capture one 15-minute high-frequency micro-burst to probe tail behavior.

On test access: a dedicated test key + IP allowlist works best. We can accept a signed test addendum (I'll loop in legal if you prefer).

Probe deliverables from Redwood
- Raw probe logs (per-request timing), aggregated p50/p95/p99, and a short note describing which runtime knobs we exercised (batch caps, chunk aggregation, cache prefixing).
- A quick-hosted-fit matrix (attached: hosted-fit-quick-matrix.xlsx) that maps observed gaps to recommended runtime changes and expected delta.

Small ask before we run: can you confirm the token-length sample size (we request a small sample of 200 requests evenly sampled across your 3 buckets) and the endpoint URL for the incumbent comparison if you want Redwood to run both legs.

I’ll prepare the smoke harness and a post-probe template so your SREs can quickly scan results.

Thanks — Naomi
